scope: Source-only ControllerHandler combined queued input capacity policy design; no implementation
proposed_policy: After existing stopped, request-length and queue-slot checks, checked request.capacity + spare.capacity > Q*L or overflow returns existing InvalidConfig; temporary aggregate byte pressure returns Busy. Accepted buffers move without copying or forced shrink. A per-job RAII charge releases when actor removes the job or queue owner drops.
compatibility: No new public enum variant, but some valid-length inputs previously accepted return InvalidConfig, and some jobs with free queue slots return Busy under byte pressure. Existing Error::InvalidConfig docs and method docs must state the input-capacity condition; race behavior is not established equivalent.
scope_boundary: The proposed Q*L limit covers queued request and spare Vec capacities and transient byte charges only. Caller-owned unpolled/admission-waiting futures, pre-byte-reservation callers, the single active job, generated responses, completed reply futures, allocator/queue metadata, kernel buffers and RSS remain outside it.
checks: Re-ran static source verifier against exact pinned repo files and Python sequential model covering error ordering, full-vs-byte pressure, exact budget, zero buffers and checked-overflow cases.
Inspected Tokio 1.53.3 try_send and try_reserve/Permit::send source, existing Controller Handler return path, tests and transport mapping of all Handler errors.
test_plan: README lists deterministic small mailbox, concurrent accounting, cancellation/shutdown, response reuse, test-gated real election WAL and positive durable vote controls; none has been implemented or executed.
limitations: Design only: no Rust patch, compiler, Cargo, native test, actor/WAL execution, network or benchmark.
New failure outcomes are unavoidable under the chosen bound and reuse/no-copy constraints; this is not a drop-in behavioral compatibility guarantee.
The Python model is sequential and does not establish the atomic counter, mpsc race, shutdown/cancellation or allocator behavior.
No total process bound, production-readiness or fastest-performance claim.
